results.title: Active route choice to minimize pedestrian thermal discomfort in a high-density subtropical city - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Active route choice to minimize pedestrian thermal discomfort in a high-density subtropical city. An active bioclimatic route choice framework is proposed to reduce pedestrian heat exposure. Thermally-driven routes reduce discomfort by up to 96 % compared to shortest paths. Shade alone is insufficient as a criterion for route choice to reduce thermal discomfort. Overheating of cities is becoming increasingly critical due to the combined effects of urban heat islands and global climate change, impacting walkability and public health, particularly in high-density tropical or subtropical cities. This study proposes an active route bioclimatic choice framework that minimizes pedestrian heat exposure and discomfort. Using high-resolution microclimate simulation and exhaustive path generation, over 2.2 million pedestrian routes were created for 1200 origin-destination (O-D) pairs in a densely populated district of subtropical Hong Kong. Results show that thermally-driven routes outperform shortest routes for 81 % of the O-D pairs, reducing thermal discomfort by up to 96 %.
